summary: 沙漠的边界并不固定，缺少植被时，风更容易带走表土。过度放牧、砍树和冲突导致的迁移都会加剧土地退化；应对措施既涉及土地管理，也涉及居民的生计。

paragraphs.brief: 气候与地貌如何界定沙漠
sentences: A desert refers to a barren section of land, mainly in arid and semi-arid areas, where there is almost no precipitation and the environment is hostile for any creature to inhabit.
沙漠是多见于干旱和半干旱地区的贫瘠土地，降水极少，生存条件严酷。
Deserts have been classified in a number of ways, generally combining total precipitation, how many days the rainfall occurs, temperature, humidity, and sometimes additional factors.
沙漠以多种方式分类，一般结合总降水量、降雨天数、温度、湿度，有时还加上其他因素。
In some places, deserts have clear boundaries marked by rivers, mountains or other landforms, while in other places there are no clear-cut borders between deserts and other landscape features.
在一些地方，沙漠有河流、山地或其他地形的清晰边界，而在另一些地方，沙漠与其他地貌特征之间没有明确的边界。
paragraphs.gist: 沙漠降水稀少，但分类时还要参考降雨天数、气温和湿度，有些沙漠以河流或山脉为界，有些则逐渐过渡到其他地貌。

paragraphs.brief: 沙尘颗粒如何引发连锁碰撞
sentences: In arid areas where there is no covering of vegetation to protect the land, sand and dust storms frequently take place.
在没有植被保护土地的干旱地区，经常发生沙尘暴。
This phenomenon often occurs along the desert margins rather than within the deserts, where there is already no finer material left.
沙尘暴常见于沙漠边缘，因为沙漠内部可被风扬起的细小颗粒已所剩无几。
When a steady wind starts to blow, fine particles on the open ground begin vibrating.
当稳定的风开始吹动，细粒子在开放的地面开始振动。
As the wind picks up, some of the particles are lifted into the air.
随着风势增强，一些颗粒被吹到空中。
When they fall onto the ground, they hit other particles, which are then jerked into the air in their turn, initiating a chain reaction.
当它们掉到地上时，它们会撞到其他粒子，然后它们被打入空气中，引发连锁反应。
paragraphs.gist: 沙漠边缘裸露的细颗粒被风带起，落地时又撞起其他颗粒，反复发生的碰撞使沙尘越扬越多。

sentences: There has been a great deal of publicity about how severe desertification can be, but the academic circle has never agreed on its causes.
有关荒漠化可能有多严重的问题已经广为人知，但学术界从未就荒漠化的原因达成一致。
A common misunderstanding is that a shortage of precipitation causes desertification—yet land in some barren areas will soon recover after rain falls.
人们常误以为荒漠化源于缺雨，可有些荒地降雨后不久便会恢复。
In fact, more often than not, human activities are responsible.
事实上，人类活动往往负有责任。
It is widely accepted that the explosion in world population, especially in developing countries, is the primary cause of soil degradation and desertification.
人们广泛认为，世界人口，特别是发展中国家人口的爆炸是土壤退化和荒漠化的主要原因。
As populations become denser, the cultivation of crops has expanded into progressively drier areas.
人口越密集，人们就越需要把作物种到更加干旱的地区。
These regions are especially likely to go through periods of severe drought, which explains why crop failures are common.
这些地区特别可能经历严重干旱时期，这解释了作物歉收很常见的原因。

The raising of most crops requires the natural vegetation cover to be removed first; when crop failures occur, extensive tracts of land are left devoid of plant cover and thus susceptible to wind and water erosion.
种植大多数作物需要首先清除自然植被；当作物歉收发生时，大片土地没有植被，因此容易受到风蚀和水蚀。
Throughout the 1990s, dry-land areas experienced a population growth of 18.5 per cent, mostly in severely impoverished developing countries.
20 世纪 90 年代，旱地人口增长了 18.5%，新增人口主要集中在十分贫困的发展中国家。
paragraphs.gist: 人口增长迫使农田向更干旱的地带扩张，一旦歉收，失去植被保护的土地便易受风蚀和水蚀，人类活动由此加速荒漠化。

paragraphs.brief: 过度放牧破坏地表草层
sentences: Livestock farming in semi-arid areas accelerates soil erosion and becomes one of the reasons for advancing desertification.
半干旱地区的畜牧业加速了土壤侵蚀，成为荒漠化加剧的原因之一。
In such areas, where the vegetation is dominated by grasses, the breeding of livestock is a major economic activity.
在植被以草为主的地区，饲养牲畜是一项主要的经济活动。
Grasses are necessary for anchoring barren topsoil in a dry-land area.
草是将贫瘠的表土固定在旱地地区所必需的。

When a specific field is used to graze an excessive herd, it loses vegetation cover, and the soil is trampled as well as pulverised, leaving the topsoil exposed to destructive forces such as wind and unexpected thunderstorms.
一片草地若放养过多牲畜，植被会被吃光，泥土也会被踩碎，表土很容易被风吹走或被突发雷暴带来的雨水冲刷。
For centuries, nomads have grazed their flocks and herds wherever pasture could be found, and oases have offered opportunities for a more settled way of living.
几个世纪以来，游牧民在可以找到牧场的地方放牧羊群和牧群，绿洲为更定居的生活提供了机会。
For some nomads, wherever they move, the desert follows.
对于一些游牧民来说，无论他们迁徙到哪里，沙漠就跟着他们。
paragraphs.gist: 半干旱地区的草根原能固定表土，牲畜过多既吃掉草层又踩碎土壤，裸露的地面更容易随风流失或被暴雨冲走。

paragraphs.brief: 采伐薪柴削弱挡风能力
sentences: Trees are of great importance when it comes to maintaining topsoil and slowing down wind speed.
树木对于维持表土和减慢风速非常重要。
In many Asian countries, firewood is the chief fuel used for cooking and heating, which has caused uncontrolled clear-cutting of forests in dry-land ecosystems.
在许多亚洲国家，木柴是用于烹饪和取暖的主要燃料，导致旱地生态系统森林无节制地被砍伐。
When too many trees are cut down, windstorms and dust storms tend to occur.
树木被过量砍伐后，强风和沙尘暴更容易发生。
paragraphs.gist: 一些亚洲国家依赖木柴做饭取暖，过量伐木使旱地失去树木固定表土、降低风速的保护，风暴和沙尘暴随之增多。

paragraphs.brief: 战争迁移带来的耕作压力
sentences: What is worse, political conflicts and wars can also contribute to desertification.
更糟糕的是，政治冲突和战争也可能导致荒漠化。
To escape invading enemies, refugees often move into some of the most vulnerable ecosystems on the planet.
为了逃离入侵的敌人，难民往往进入地球上一些最脆弱的生态系统。
They bring along their traditional cultivation practices, which may not be suitable for their new settlements.
他们带来了传统的耕作做法，这些做法可能不适合他们的新定居点。
paragraphs.gist: 战争会迫使难民迁入脆弱的生态区，原居地的耕作方式若不适合当地，也可能加剧土地荒漠化。

paragraphs.brief: 用新生计减轻土地压力
sentences: In the 20th century, one state in the United States had a large section of farmland that turned into desert.
20世纪，美国有一个州有大量的农田变成了沙漠
Since then, measures have been enforced so that such a phenomenon will not happen again.
自那时以来，已采取措施，使这种现象不再发生。

To avoid the recurrence of desertification, people must find livelihoods that do not rely on traditional land uses, are less demanding on local natural resources, yet can still generate viable income.
为了避免荒漠化的复发，人们必须找到不依赖传统土地使用、对当地自然资源要求较少、但仍能产生可维持收入的生计。

Such livelihoods include, but are not limited to, dry-land aquaculture for the raising of fish, crustaceans and industrial compounds derived from micro-algae, greenhouse agriculture, and activities related to tourism.
例如，可以在旱地发展水产养殖，饲养鱼虾或利用微藻生产工业化合物，也可以发展温室农业和旅游业。
Another way to prevent desertification is to create economic prospects in the city centres of dry-lands and in areas outside them.
另一条途径是在旱地的城镇中心及外围地区创造就业和发展机会。
Changing the wider economic and institutional structures so that people have new ways to support themselves would help alleviate the pressures that drive desertification.
改变更广泛的经济和体制结构，使人们有新的方式养活自己，将有助于减轻驱动荒漠化的压力。
paragraphs.gist: 要避免农田再次变成沙漠，可发展旱地水产养殖、温室农业和旅游，并在城镇创造就业机会，减少居民对土地的依赖。

paragraphs.brief: 卫星如何帮助观察荒漠化
sentences: In today’s society, new technologies are being used to address the problems brought about by desertification.
在当今的社会中，新技术正被用来解决荒漠化带来的问题。
Satellites, for example, have been utilised to investigate the influence that people and livestock have on our planet.
例如，卫星被用来调查人和牲畜对我们星球的影响。
However, this does not mean that alternative technologies are not needed to help tackle the processes of desertification.
然而，这并不意味着不需要替代技术来帮助解决荒漠化进程。
paragraphs.gist: 卫星已能帮助研究人类和牲畜对环境的影响，但应对荒漠化仍需要其他技术配合。

items.en: a reference to the irregular movement of particles
items.zh: 提及粒子的不规则移动
items.why: 风吹起的颗粒落地又撞起其他颗粒，引发连锁运动，描述了沙粒如何不规则地跃动。

items.en: mention of productive land turning into desert in the 20th century
items.zh: 提到在20世纪肥沃的土地变成沙漠
items.why: G段开头就举出二十世纪美国一个州大片农田变成沙漠的例子。
A段说明沙漠可以按降水量、降水天数、气温和湿度等因素分类。

items.en: mention of technical methods used to tackle the problems of deserts
items.zh: 提到处理沙漠问题所使用的技术方法
items.why: H段举出卫星监测人类与牲畜对土地的影响，是用技术研究荒漠化的方法。

items.en: the influence of migration on desertification
items.why: 逃避战乱的人迁入脆弱地区，让当地承受额外的土地利用压力，说明迁移与荒漠化的联系。

items.en: lack of agreement among scientists about the causes of desertification
items.zh: 科学家对荒漠化的原因缺乏共识
items.why: 段落 C 首句“the academic circle has never agreed on its causes”直接表明科学家在成因上缺乏共识。

items.en: a description of the harmful effects of farming practices
items.zh: 描述某些农业生产方式对土地的损害
items.why: 段落 D 详细说明过度放牧使“topsoil…trampled and pulverised, leaving the topsoil exposed”,述畜牧耕作方式带来的有害后果。

items.en: It is difficult to ascertain where deserts end in some areas.
items.zh: 很难确定某些地区沙漠的尽头。
items.why: 有些沙漠以河山为界，另一些却没有清晰分界，因此部分地区难以判定边缘。

items.en: The media is uninterested in the problems of desertification.
items.zh: 媒体对荒漠化问题不感兴趣。
items.why: 文章说荒漠化的严重性已经获得大量宣传，与媒体不感兴趣相反。

items.en: The most common cause of desertification is a lack of rainfall.
items.zh: 荒漠化最常见的原因是缺乏降雨。
items.why: 作者把简单归因于少雨称为常见误解，并指出一些看似贫瘠的地带降雨后很快恢复。

items.en: Farming animals in semi-arid areas will increase soil erosion.
items.zh: 在半干旱地区饲养牲畜会加剧土壤侵蚀。
items.why: D段直接指出半干旱地区养牲畜会加速土壤侵蚀，符合题干。

items.en: People in Asian countries no longer use firewood as their chief fuel.
items.zh: 亚洲国家的人民不再用木柴作为主要燃料。
items.why: 在许多亚洲国家，木柴仍是烹饪和取暖的主要燃料，所以不能说它已不再是主要燃料。

items.en: Technology for studying the relationship between people, livestock and desertification has not yet been invented.
items.zh: 研究人、牲畜和荒漠化之间关系的技术尚未发明。
items.why: 卫星已经用于研究人和牲畜对土地的影响，说明相关技术并非尚未发明。

points: 逃避战乱的人迁入脆弱地区，让当地承受额外的土地利用压力，说明迁移与荒漠化的联系。
作者把简单归因于少雨称为常见误解，并指出一些看似贫瘠的地带降雨后很快恢复。
clauses: In some places, deserts have clear boundaries marked by rivers, mountains or other landforms, ….
连接词 while 引出“while in other places there are no clear-cut borders between deserts and other landscape features”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
When they fall onto the ground, they hit other particles, …, initiating a chain reaction.
“which are then jerked into the air in their turn”修饰前面的 particles。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 particles，再把修饰信息接回主句。
